en: The island province of Camiguin has seven volcanoes, which is more than its five municipalities.
Mount Hamiguitan features a unique pygmy forest where century-old trees grow only a few feet tall.
Lake Taal is a crater lake located on Volcano Island, which sits inside another lake in Luzon.
Bohol’s Chocolate Hills consist of over 1,200 symmetrical mounds that turn chocolate brown during the dry season.
Although the Philippines is an archipelago of 7,641 islands, only about 2,000 of them are actually inhabited.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous worldwide for having one of the most perfectly symmetrical volcanic cones on Earth.
The Philippine Trench contains the Galathea Depth, which is the third deepest oceanic trench in the entire world.
Mount Pulag is famous for its sea of clouds, a thick cloud layer that sits below its grassy peak.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River is uniquely affected by ocean tides, causing saltwater to flow six kilometers inland.
The massive 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo released so much ash that it temporarily cooled the global climate.
With 7,641 islands, the Philippines is the second-largest archipelagic country in the world, right after Indonesia.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is the only landlocked region in the Philippines, meaning it has no direct ocean coastline.
